results.name: Tokyo National Museum
results.why_it_is_special: Japan's oldest and largest museum, housing national treasures and important cultural properties spanning thousands of years of Japanese and East Asian art and history.

results.name: teamLab Borderless (MORI Building Digital Art Museum)
results.why_it_is_special: The world's first all-digital art museum where artworks flow between rooms without boundaries. Visitors become part of the immersive, interactive experience — no fixed routes or maps.

results.name: Nezu Museum
results.why_it_is_special: Houses over 7,000 works of pre-modern Japanese and East Asian art — including national treasures — collected by businessman Nezu Kaichirō. Set within a serene traditional Japanese garden designed by architect Kengo Kuma.

results.name: Mori Art Museum
results.why_it_is_special: A leading contemporary art museum perched atop the 53rd floor of Roppongi Hills Mori Tower, offering world-class exhibitions alongside panoramic views of the Tokyo skyline.

results.name: The National Art Centre, Tokyo (NACT)
results.why_it_is_special: Japan's largest exhibition space (14,000 m²) with no permanent collection — instead hosting a rotating programme of diverse art shows. The undulating glass façade by Kisho Kurokawa is an architectural landmark in its own right.

results.name: Senso-ji Temple
results.why_it_is_special: Tokyo's oldest Buddhist temple, originally founded in 645 CE. The iconic Kaminarimon (Thunder Gate), Nakamise shopping street, five-storey pagoda, and main hall form a stunning complex at the heart of historic Asakusa.

results.name: Meiji Jingū Shrine
results.why_it_is_special: A Shinto shrine dedicated to Emperor Meiji and Empress Shōken, set within a 70-hectare forested sanctuary that offers a tranquil retreat from the surrounding city. Adjacent to Yoyogi Park and the Harajuku shopping district.

results.name: Tokyo Skytree
results.why_it_is_special: Japan's tallest structure at 634 metres, completed in 2012. A testament to modern Japanese architectural ambition, with observation decks offering sweeping views of the entire metropolitan area.

results.name: Tsukiji Outer Market
results.why_it_is_special: A vibrant open-air market that preserves Tokyo's culinary heritage — fresh seafood, street food, wagyu beef, traditional rice crackers, and seasonal produce. A living celebration of Japanese food culture and community.

results.name: Nakamise Shopping Street
results.why_it_is_special: A 250-metre-long traditional shopping arcade leading to Senso-ji Temple, lined with stalls selling souvenirs, street food, and crafts — a tradition dating back centuries when vendors served pilgrims walking to the temple.

results.name: Yanaka Ginza (Yanesen district)
results.why_it_is_special: One of Tokyo's best-preserved old-town neighbourhoods, featuring nostalgic Shōwa-era streetscapes, small temples, traditional sweet shops, and retro shopping streets — a rare window into pre-war Tokyo daily life.

results.name: Suginami Animation Museum
results.why_it_is_special: A free museum dedicated to the history of Japanese animation (anime), with exhibits, production workshops, and talks by industry professionals — ideal for understanding Japan's globally influential anime culture.
